questions.stem: Foreign policy is best defined as

options.text: the strategy a state adopts in its relations with other states to protect its national interest
the law that governs local government markets
the manifesto of a registered political party
the procedure for amending a rigid constitution

questions.explanation: Foreign policy is outward-facing: how a sovereign state deals with other states and international organisations. Nigeria's stated aims — security, economic interest, African unity, international peace — are instances of national interest, not of local administration or party programmes.

distractorRationale.b: Market regulation is a Fourth Schedule local-government function, not foreign policy
distractorRationale.c: A manifesto is a party's domestic programme for winning elections
distractorRationale.d: Amendment procedure is constitutional law, not diplomacy

questions.stem: Which of the following is a determinant, rather than an instrument, of foreign policy?

options.text: Sending an ambassador to a foreign capital
Deploying troops on a peacekeeping mission
A country's geography and the structure of its economy
Imposing trade sanctions on another state

questions.explanation: Determinants are the conditions that shape what a state can want and can do: location, oil or the lack of it, population, military capacity, leadership, public opinion, history. Ambassadors, troops and sanctions are instruments — tools used after those conditions have already framed the choice.

distractorRationale.a: An ambassador is a diplomatic instrument

questions.stem: The principle that Africa is the centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy is illustrated by

options.text: Nigeria's leading role in ECOMOG and its support for the anti-apartheid struggle
the creation of 774 local government areas
the introduction of the Clifford Constitution in 1922
the anonymity of the civil service

questions.explanation: Afrocentrism means African questions come first. ECOMOG in Liberia and Sierra Leone, support for liberation movements, and the campaign against apartheid are the standard illustrations. Local government, colonial constitutions and civil-service principles are domestic topics.

distractorRationale.b: 774 councils are a fact of Nigerian local government, not of foreign policy
distractorRationale.d: Anonymity is a feature of the civil service

questions.stem: During the Cold War, Nigeria's official stance of not becoming a satellite of either East or West was called

options.text: apartheid
non-alignment
indirect rule
proportional representation

questions.explanation: Non-alignment, associated with the Non-Aligned Movement, meant refusing membership of the NATO or Warsaw Pact camps while remaining free to deal with both. Nigeria treated it as compatible with an Africa-first policy. Apartheid, indirect rule and PR are different concepts altogether.

distractorRationale.a: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial domination, which Nigeria opposed
distractorRationale.c: Indirect rule was the British colonial administrative method
distractorRationale.d: Proportional representation is an electoral system

questions.stem: ECOMOG is best classified among the instruments of Nigerian foreign policy as a

options.text: purely cultural instrument, like a film festival
military instrument used for regional peacekeeping and peace enforcement
domestic instrument for collecting local rates
judicial instrument of the International Court of Justice

questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group was a regional military force, dominated and largely financed by Nigeria, first deployed to Liberia in 1990. It is the stock example of Nigeria using the military instrument in pursuit of an Afrocentric objective. It is not a cultural festival, a tax office or a UN court.

distractorRationale.a: Culture can be an instrument (Nollywood, sport), but ECOMOG was an armed mission
distractorRationale.c: Rate collection is a local-government revenue function
distractorRationale.d: The ICJ is a principal organ of the UN, not ECOMOG

questions.stem: Nigeria's campaign against apartheid in South Africa is an example of the Africa-as-centrepiece principle.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Treating white-minority rule in South Africa as Nigeria's own diplomatic business — through boycotts, funds, UN activism and support for liberation movements — is a classic Afrocentric policy. It placed an African racial-justice struggle above any extra-African alignment.

distractorRationale.b: Denying the link usually comes from treating anti-apartheid as 'world politics' rather than as African policy, which is the opposite of Nigeria's official doctrine
